newsitem.title: UK: Sugar freight market quiet, Far East still active.
newsitem.headline: Sugar freight market quiet, Far East still active.

text.p: Business slackened off on the sugar freight market at the end of the week but the Far East market remained busy, shipbrokers said on Friday.
E D & F Man fixed 12,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Thailand to Indonesia for mid-February, with the rate reported between $15.00 and $15.25.
Man was also said to have also fixed a further 14,000 tonnes in bags from Coatzacoalcos or Veracruz to Colombo for prompt shipment dates.
Shipbrokers said Sugar Chartering Inc fixed 24,000/25,000 tonnes of bulk sugar on subjects from Philippines to US Gulf/Atlantic for prompt dates.
Of the day's new inquiry, Louis Dreyfus was open for 13,200/14,300 tonnes of bagged sugar from Thailand to Indonesia for the end of February.
Benham or nominee was in the market for 14,000 tonnes min/max bagged sugar from Puerto Quetzal to Valparaiso for the second half of February.
Shipbrokers said Amerop was looking for a tonnage to ship 18,000/25,000 tonnes in bulk from the Philippines to US Gulf/Atlantic or California for end February/early March.
